mission.title: Install and Configure Prometheus Operator / kube-prometheus-stack
mission.description: The Prometheus Operator simplifies the deployment and management of Prometheus monitoring stacks on Kubernetes. It allows users to configure Prometheus and related components using Kubernetes custom resources, making it easier to manage monitoring configurations. Key trade-offs include the need for familiarity with Kubernetes resources and potential complexity in advanced configurations.

steps.title: Add the Prometheus Operator Helm repository
steps.description:
This step adds the official Prometheus Operator Helm chart repository to your Helm configuration.

```bash

helm repo add prometheus-community https://prometheus-community.github.io/helm-charts

helm repo update

```

> This is the official repository for Prometheus Operator.
> Updates the local Helm chart repository cache.

steps.title: Install the Prometheus Operator
steps.description:
This command installs the Prometheus Operator using Helm, specifying the namespace and version.

```bash

kubectl create namespace monitoring

helm install prometheus-operator prometheus-community/kube-prometheus-stack --namespace monitoring --version 0.77.0

```

> Creates a namespace for the monitoring stack.
> Installs the kube-prometheus-stack with the specified version.

steps.title: Verify the installation
steps.description:
This step checks that the Prometheus Operator and its components are running correctly.

```bash

kubectl get pods -n monitoring

kubectl get svc -n monitoring

```

> Lists all pods in the monitoring namespace to verify their status.
> Lists all services in the monitoring namespace to ensure they are created.

steps.title: Create a Prometheus custom resource
steps.description:
This command creates a sample Prometheus resource to start monitoring your applications.

```bash

cat <<EOF | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: monitoring.coreos.com/v1
kind: Prometheus
metadata:
  name: example-prometheus
  namespace: monitoring
spec:
  replicas: 1
  serviceAccountName: prometheus-operator
  serviceMonitorSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: my-app
EOF

```

> Creates a basic Prometheus instance.

uninstall.title: Uninstall the Prometheus Operator
uninstall.description:
This step removes the Prometheus Operator and all associated resources. Be aware that this will delete all monitoring data and configurations.

```bash

helm uninstall prometheus-operator --namespace monitoring

kubectl delete namespace monitoring

```

> Uninstalls the Prometheus Operator.
> Deletes the monitoring namespace and all its resources.

upgrade.title: Upgrade the Prometheus Operator
upgrade.description:
Before upgrading, ensure you backup your Prometheus data and configurations. This step will upgrade the Prometheus Operator to the latest version.

```bash

kubectl get prometheus -n monitoring -o yaml > prometheus-backup.yaml

helm upgrade prometheus-operator prometheus-community/kube-prometheus-stack --namespace monitoring --version 0.77.0

kubectl get pods -n monitoring

```

> Backs up the current Prometheus configuration.
> Upgrades the Prometheus Operator to the specified version.
> Verifies that all pods are running after the upgrade.

troubleshooting.title: Error: 'Error creating service monitor: ServiceMonitor.monitoring.coreos.com "example" is invalid'
troubleshooting.description:
**Cause:** This error occurs when the ServiceMonitor resource is not correctly configured or the target service does not exist.

**Fix:**
Check the ServiceMonitor configuration and ensure the target service is running.

troubleshooting.title: Prometheus pod is in 'CrashLoopBackOff' state
troubleshooting.description:
**Cause:** This can happen due to misconfiguration in the Prometheus custom resource or insufficient resources.

**Fix:**
Check the logs of the Prometheus pod using 'kubectl logs <pod-name> -n monitoring' and adjust the configuration or resources as needed.

troubleshooting.title: Alertmanager not receiving alerts
troubleshooting.description:
**Cause:** This may occur if the alerting rules are not configured correctly or the Alertmanager service is not reachable.

**Fix:**
Verify the alerting rules and check the connectivity to the Alertmanager service.

troubleshooting.title: ServiceMonitor not discovering targets
troubleshooting.description:
**Cause:** This can happen if the labels on the target services do not match the selectors defined in the ServiceMonitor.

**Fix:**
Ensure that the labels on the target services match the selectors in the ServiceMonitor configuration.
